brief.headline: Push 16.6% price cut on PET bottles to match Suraj Blow Plast and offer faster payment for another point or two off

priceAsk.summary: Drop the PET bottle price from ₹2.18/NOS to ₹1.87/NOS — a 16.6% cut
priceAsk.basis: We already pay Suraj Blow Plast ₹1.87/NOS for the same PET BOT AMBER 100ML/25MM NECK 12.5G bottle. TPAC is 16.6% higher. Closing that gap saves us ₹28644 a year. The market also shows modest room down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume for caps, so their current pricing has headroom.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days after receipt to paying on delivery, in exchange for 1–2% off the price
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹46539 for us; 30 days faster (on delivery) frees up ₹93078

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC is healthy — rated [ICRA] A / Stable, they keep ₹3.80 of every ₹100 they sell (net margin 3.8%), and they borrow money at about 10.27%. Their cash is stuck for 79 days (same as similar firms at 79 days), so cash isn't super-tight but early payment is still worth roughly 10% a year to them. We're tiny — just 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue — so on our own we have almost no pull. The play is to bundle this SKU with other rigid-plastic buys, commit longer term, or quietly line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek and let TPAC know we're qualifying a second source.

evidence.point: We pay Suraj Blow Plast ₹1.87/NOS for the identical PET bottle; TPAC charges ₹2.18/NOS
Closing that 16.6% gap saves us ₹28644 a year
TPAC borrows at about 10.27%, so paying 30 days early is worth roughly that rate to them
We're only 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr sales — we need to bundle volume or show an alternate to get their attention
They have GST filing delays and EPF payment delays on record
evidence.figure: GST filing delays, EPF payment delays

evidence.point: Market reference for 28 mm PP caps shows typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc, modest room down to ₹0.65–0.80 at scale

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue), does pharma bottles and caps — the top second-source candidate; health score B (65/100)

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr), strong and profitable (health B 73/100), makes pails, containers and pharma packaging — a robust backup for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle and jar specialist (Pearlpet brand, ₹19.83 Cr) — direct fit for our PET bottles, though smaller and weaker (health D 32/100)

risks: We're only 0.02% of their business, so they may ignore us unless we bundle more SKUs or commit longer term
GST filing delays and EPF payment delays are on their record — watch for any supply hiccups or compliance issues that could disrupt our line
Their Altman Z-score is 2.77 (grey zone) — not in distress but not bulletproof either; don't squeeze so hard you tip a fragile supplier, especially since we're so small to them
If we move too much volume to an alternate too fast, TPAC may not care — make sure the second source is qualified and can actually deliver before you play that card
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're paying Suraj Blow Plast ₹1.87 for the same bottle you're charging us ₹2.18 for — let's close that 16.6% gap and talk about how paying you faster can earn us another point or two off.
